answer: A farm running 80 keys hence burns for 80 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the lagoon declaration. Because the walnut audit recomputes usage from the quill history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 536 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
